function: MASAC agents learn terminal uplink transmit power and UAV flight direction and speed for NOMA offloading to UAV edge servers, maximizing long-term sensing rate (pp. 7-8).
system: UAV-enabled MEC network: 3 UAVs at 100 m, 45 terminals, NOMA uplink, 1 MHz band, 0.1 GHz carrier, 1000x1000 m, antennas not stated, no RIS (pp. 4, 11).
method: Multi-agent soft actor-critic (AGIN-MASAC): one agent per UAV and terminal, fully connected actor and twin Q-critics; reinforcement learning, trained over episodes with replay (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Custom simulation: free-space path loss plus LoS/NLoS losses with environment-based LoS probability, NOMA co-channel interference; no standardized, public, or measured data (pp. 4, 11).
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated in one simulated 1000x1000 m scenario; results swept over task size, terminal count, UAV computing capacity; no unseen-scenario test stated (pp. 11-13).
baselines: MADDPG [4] (learned); PSO for UAV resource allocation (non-learned); NT-MASAC with fixed concentric UAV trajectory; NP-MASAC with maximum terminal power (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Sum accumulative reward, average data sensing rate, queuing delay, terminal throughput, terminal energy consumption, block creation delay (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Big-O orders: SP1 O(I1 K), MASAC training over episodes, slots, agents and layer sizes, DOA O(I_DOA N0 J K), and their sum; online inference stated negligible (p. 10).
openness: none; the only link (footnote 2, p. 7) hosts the proof appendix, not code or data.
q1_support: p. 4: "is the LoS probability for the link" from terminal to UAV, part of a custom free-space plus LoS/NLoS path-loss model (Table III, p. 11). No 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 13: "the number of terminal devices increases" describes a sweep (Fig. 10). The paper does not state that an agent trained in one scenario was tested in a different one.
q3_support: p. 11: "3) MADDPG [4]: Terminal data sensing rate and UAV" (learned, same functions); p. 11: "assumed to follow a series of concentric circles for" (fixed trajectory), plus PSO for resource allocation; p. 13: "36.27%, 15.41%, and 13.16% compared to the NT-MASAC," gives sensing-rate gains.
q4_support: p. 10: "SP1 is a convex subproblem, optimized through I1 iterations" with order O(I1 K); the same section gives the MASAC training order and the DOA order O(I_DOA N0 J K).
q5_support: p. 7: "Proof: See Appendix A.2" whose footnote 2 is the only link (a Baidu Netdisk address) and hosts the appendix, not code or data; p. 11: "Consider a 1000 m" simulated area, no public dataset.
notes: Borderline on the physical-layer test: the objective is MEC and blockchain level (sensing rate under queue and block-delay limits), and sensing admission, UAV computing allocation, and trajectory sit above the physical layer. It passes only through the learned terminal transmit-power control on aerial links, which the instructions count as physical layer, so area 6; the reviewer may confirm. The Baidu link in footnote 2 (p. 7) is for Appendix A, so q5 is 0. q3 counts MADDPG [4] as the learned baseline and the fixed circular trajectory, maximum power, and PSO as non-learned.
